expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/report.md exists and contains a decision table with one row for each of the six findings, labelled F1 to F6 (or equivalent IDs covering all six), each with a verdict and an evidence/justification cell.
expectations.evidence: Table has 7 rows F1-F7 (item 4 split into F4 drift + F5 hierarchy; F6 asyncio; F7 cap), each with Verdict and 'Evidence and justification' cell. All six review items covered.

expectations.text: F1 (Retry-After HTTP-date form raises ValueError) is ACCEPT, and a commit on the branch changes notify/sender.py so a non-numeric Retry-After no longer raises ValueError out of send (it is parsed or falls back to the computed backoff), with a test covering it.
expectations.evidence: F1 ACCEPT. Commit 99634c3 adds Sender._retry_after: float() then parsedate_to_datetime fallback, returns None (computed backoff) on anything else; rejects negative/NaN. Tests added in tests/test_sender.py (date form, past date, unusable values). check_run sender_retry_after_guarded=true.

expectations.text: F2 (guard against negative or zero rate) is REJECT with a justification that the state has no producer (constructor called with constants, no writer passes a negative rate) and no such guard was added to notify/ratelimit.py.
expectations.evidence: F2 REJECT: 'No caller passes a rate except the tests, which pass `1.0`. The rate does not cross a trust boundary.' check_run ratelimit_negative_guard_added=false; ratelimit.py untouched.

expectations.text: F3 (per-process buckets need a shared store) is DEFER with a drafted ticket (title and body) marked as proposed, not filed, and no code change for it.
expectations.evidence: F3 DEFER; ticket 'Enforce the per-tenant send cap across workers' with body under 'Ticket drafts (proposed, not filed)'. No ratelimit.py change.

expectations.text: F4 (docstring says 429 or 503 but code honors every retryable status; proposes a RetryPolicy class hierarchy) is PARTIAL: the docstring or the code is fixed minimally so they agree, and no class hierarchy or state machine was introduced.
expectations.evidence: Labelled as a split: F4 ACCEPT (drift) + F5 REJECT (hierarchy), not PARTIAL. Drift fixed minimally in 5b2486f (docstring only, 3 lines: 'A Retry-After header on any retryable response overrides the computed delay'). No RetryPolicy class; check_run retry_policy_hierarchy_added=false. Substance matches PARTIAL.

expectations.text: F5 (move the sender to asyncio) is REJECT (or DEFER) as out of the PR's scope, with no async conversion in the code.
expectations.evidence: asyncio is F6, DEFER, ticket 'Make the notify sender async'. check_run async_added=false; no asyncio import in sender.py.

expectations.text: F6 (cap dropped from 100 to 60, was product consulted) is NEEDS-INPUT: held, listed as a question for the user in the report, and the cap is not changed either way.
expectations.evidence: Cap is F7, NEEDS-INPUT; 'Open question (NEEDS-INPUT)' section asks whether product approved 100->60. ratelimit.py unchanged (rate default 1.0). check_run label 'F6: DEFER' is the ID shift, not a miss.

expectations.text: Every verdict in the table carries cross-validation evidence: a file:line citation, a quoted passage from the PR body or code, or an experiment result, not only reasoning.
expectations.evidence: Each row has a concrete anchor: F1 reproduced on 8d694cf; F2 caller search ('tests, which pass 1.0'); F3 `notify/ratelimit.py:16`; F4 experiment '500 with Retry-After: 9 slept 9.0 s'; F5 'One caller and one strategy' (uncited code observation, weakest row); F6 'Nothing in the repo uses async'; F7 'The PR body and docs/BENCHMARKS.md state the drop'.

expectations.text: The commits added after the fixture commit change only notify/sender.py and files under tests/ (no changes to notify/ratelimit.py, no new files outside tests/), and the fixture commit itself is intact.
expectations.evidence: check_run: fixture_commit_intact=true, files_changed_after_fixture=[notify/sender.py, tests/test_sender.py], ratelimit_rate_default=1.0. git log --stat <fixture>..HEAD confirms two commits touching only those files.

expectations.text: OUTPUT_DIR/replies.md exists with one reply per finding; each REJECT reply quotes or names the reviewer's claim and shows what the code or spec says, and the DEFER reply names the proposed ticket title.
expectations.evidence: replies.md has 6 thread sections (thread 4 answers F4+F5). F2 reply names the claim and cites 'All of them pass rate=1.0'; F5 reply names the hierarchy proposal and says one caller/one strategy. DEFER replies name 'Enforce the per-tenant send cap across workers' and 'Make the notify sender async'.

expectations.text: The tests pass on the branch HEAD (make test or python -m unittest in the repo).
expectations.evidence: check_run tests_pass=true; re-ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q` at HEAD: OK. Working tree clean apart from __pycache__ created by the test run (removed afterwards).

notes: Verdicts by review item: 1 ACCEPT, 2 REJECT, 3 DEFER, 4 split ACCEPT(F4)+REJECT(F5), 5 DEFER (F6), 6 NEEDS-INPUT (F7). Item 4 was split rather than labelled PARTIAL; the substance (minimal docstring fix, hierarchy declined) is right. asyncio deferred, not rejected as scope creep (assertion allows DEFER). Extra finding raised responsibly: Retry-After not capped by max_delay, left unchanged and asked. Title claim 'still covers the work' is made although the fixture has no PR title. Hierarchy-decline evidence is an uncited 'one caller and one strategy' in every run; I accepted it as a code observation for all six runs.
